turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports the council just sent congress a 2027 revenue law of 6,746 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Nine percent less than this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Own-source revenue would fall nearly 20 percent, and they warn projects may get cut.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The city points to the cooling real estate market.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the same time Diario Humano says residents will collect signatures 19 to 22 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Under the slogan The Coastal Road stays.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They want the East Cape route kept in the 2040 plan as a rustic scenic drive with beach access.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At the same time residents are gathering signatures to keep the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The earlier update would have dropped 3.9 km of the 94 km route.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Grupo Questro wants a highway set back at least one kilometre from the beach.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today we dive into Infrastructure, and the question we chase is: what is a road for when the budget shrinks?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports Los Cabos sent a 2027 revenue law of 6,746 million pesos to the state congress.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is down from 7,421 million this year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 9.09% less. Own revenue from property taxes and fees drops nearly 20% less. The city points to the cooling real estate market and says some works may be cut.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Who feels that first?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano says residents launch a signature drive this week to keep the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They want the rustic route to stay.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. A private proposal would move any new highway a kilometer inland. Implan prefers a scenic drive with beach access. The mayor promises consultation.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens if three point nine kilometers disappear from the map?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports rain and a sewage spill have damaged the Transpeninsular highway shoulders between San José and Cabo San Lucas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The water utility has not fixed the spill in over 20 days.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: SCT confirms the damage and calls for a full assessment that includes drainage.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And in La Paz?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México notes the rebuild of Agustín Arriola street starts today with hydraulic concrete, from Paseo Álvaro Obregón to Francisco I. Madero.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meant to bring commerce and visitors back to the center.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The road closes at six. Residents moved their cars last night.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What does a road teach a city about its own future?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The news keeps circling back to pipes and roads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tribuna de México reports Los Cabos shut 25 illegal water connections this year. Theft above 300 litres per second.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And a senator wants ten years in prison for that.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same week Palabra BCS notes La Paz is replacing water and sewer lines on Francisco King Rondero for 48 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto is doing the same on Calle Marlín. alDíaBCS says the paving there is already 45 percent complete.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Drainage and the drinking-water network come first, then the lights.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the hidden thread is the network itself.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight editions called it water-energy coupling. Desal plants and grid outages set the 2050 ceiling.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens when the sea decides the shape of the shore.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS says fishers warned since 2015 that the Tres Santos development changed beach dynamics at Punta Lobos. Part of the hotel was demolished after the waves reached the foundations.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the governor's Fifth Report lands next week. It will list every road and pipe under the five axes of the State Development Plan.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: IMCO noted BCS climbed from eighth to fifth in competitiveness. Yet the same report says decisions still happen in silos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here's the thing. The same logic that moves sand also moves water and power across five states.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A regional treaty was proposed at the summit to tie investment to the Sea of Cortez itself.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. One thread, many shores.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Did you know the second desal plant in Cabo San Lucas is now at 75 percent?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Gobierno del estado reports it will add 250 liters per second. Together the two plants reach 655 liters per second once finished in 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Imagine turning on the tap in a hotel room. That steady flow depends on these pipes and pumps.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. Water scarcity already limits new projects in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet at the Foro Mar de Cortés Summit Agustín Coppel proposed tripling regional FDI with more roads, ports and airports.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: BCS grew only 2.1 percent a year over the last decade. The desert sets the real pace.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal notes tourism investment leads the state while the same water shortage acts as a brake.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents marched to the water offices last October. They see the tension every day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city about its own growth?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Visión pillar for energy shows one clear risk.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The island grid stays the only ceiling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: SIBCS reached 689 MW peak in 2024. The portal also records 660 MW net and 675 MW for 2023. Tourism, pumping and desalination all draw from the same system.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would it take to move past that limit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The aspiration is a system with clean generation, storage and demand that respects the real ceiling. The levers are simple: finish the northern remote-generation tenders without turning them into residential permits, and plan desalination and pumping inside the grid from the start.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And the Tendencia 2050 reads a polycentric map instead of one repeated coastal line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos under stress, East Cape in tension with protected areas, Todos Santos and El Pescadero as the Pacific amenity spine, La Paz as the water-energy node, Loreto as tourism-conservation anchor, Comondú as agricultural hub, and northern Mulegé with the CFE Oasis tender now visible.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Each place keeps its own role.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. New tourism or residential growth only appears where margin is shown or from a non-DMA source like desal, without pretending NOM-011 credit. East Cape and Loreto respect ANP and POEL ceilings before scaling hospitality. Comondú and the north add production and energy without emptying services or ANPs.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And on the watchlist.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: SIBCS reliability and CFE works against OOMSAPAS supply incidents. Water theft carries a federal bill of up to 10 years in prison, with closures of illegal connections already happening in Los Cabos. The second Cabo San Lucas desal plant sits at 75 percent, 250 l/s, completion 2027. And the CFE Oasis Mulegé tender of 72 MW PV, 20 MW over 80 MWh storage, and 20 MW electrolyser.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where the series falls short, the Trend already marks it insufficient.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: After the reports and the petitions, what stays with you?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents gathered signatures to keep the East Cape Coastal Road in the 2040 plan. 25 illegal water connections turned up this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the spills on the Transpeninsular?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The small choices. A street rebuilt, a road kept in the plan, connections found and closed.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: In Loreto, Calle Marlín is nearly half paved. The desert light falls on every new layer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the desert teach a city?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The takeaway is this: infrastructure here is the quiet work of fitting growth to the desert and the coast without breaking either.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
